extracted.intended_audience: researchers/clinicians developing or validating measurement instruments and assessing interrater/intrarater reliability
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reported standards for developing, training, validating, and measuring interrater and intrarater reliability of clinical/behavioral/diagnostic instruments and automated classifiers. Covers choice of statistics, training/certification, validation procedures, and interpretation of agreement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Cohen's Kappa to quantify agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohen's kappa statistic (including weighted kappa where appropriate) is used to quantify interrater and test–retest agreement between two raters/assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report kappa values with confidence intervals; interpret using common benchmarks (e.g., moderate 0.41–0.60, substantial 0.61–0.80, almost perfect >0.80). Include item-level and overall kappas where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Fleiss' Kappa for multi-rater agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fleiss' Kappa is used to estimate interrater agreement when more than two raters review events or cases (example: majority voting on web-based EEG scoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using majority voting, compute Fleiss' Kappa to assess overall agreement; report proportions of events with high/moderate/poor agreement and relate to the resulting Kappa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICC is used to measure interrater and intrarater reliability for continuous or composite scores (example: ICC for inter-/intra-rater reliability reported for many clinical measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify ICC model (e.g., two-way random) and report 95% confidence intervals. Use ICC to assess reliability of composite/total scores and continuous measures; compare to benchmarks (e.g., >0.75 good/excellent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report percent agreement / proportion of agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of agreement (PA) or percent agreement is reported alongside kappa/ICC to show raw agreement rates (e.g., PA and κ for fracture classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PA as descriptive complement to kappa (which adjusts for chance). Where appropriate, use Chamberlain's percent positive agreement for diagnostic abstractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish interrater and intrarater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrater reliability (different raters) and intrarater (same rater over time/test–retest) should be separately assessed and reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For test–retest/intrarater reliability, allow an appropriate interval between assessments (example: at least 2 weeks) and report weighted kappa or ICC as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content validation via expert consensus (Delphi / nominal groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured expert consensus methods (Delphi, nominal groups, multi-member development teams) to create and validate level descriptions/content of classification systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the development team composition, stakeholder representation (professionals, parents, patients), and the process (number of rounds, critiques) used to establish content validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion validity / convergent validation against established measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess criterion validity by comparing new grades/scores to established instruments or outcomes (example: DIGEST vs OPSE, MBSImP, MDADI, PSS-HN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate statistics (correlations, ANOVA with post hoc comparisons) to demonstrate discrimination across grades and report significance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency and construct validity reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report internal consistency (e.g., Cronbach's alpha), factor analysis, and construct validity assessments for multi-item instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide alpha coefficients for overall scale and domains, report factor loadings, and show relationships with related constructs to support validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all possible item responses and full item coverage in training/certification materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and certification materials (e.g., NIHSS videos) should include all possible responses on individual scale items to ensure raters see the full response spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professionally produced training/certification videos and workshops; report pass rates and compare with original-language standards where cross-linguistic versions are produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training and shared scoring conventions are essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured rater training, shared scoring conventions, and certification improve interrater reliability and are often necessary for multicenter trials and clinical use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training can be in-person or web-based interactive video; include diverse examples (ages, genders, races); assess interrater reliability after training and consider repeated/booster sessions if reliability is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-based interactive video for scalable rater training
rubrics_metrics.description: Web-based interactive video systems can be used to train raters and assess their interrater reliability across sites when live training is impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use actor portrayals across demographics, standardize scoring conventions, and run reliability testing; discuss advantages (logistics) and limitations (ecological validity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Majority voting for consensus classification
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple raters review events, majority voting may be used to assign a consensus label (example: seizure/non-seizure classification based on majority votes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how many raters agreed, proportion of unanimous decisions, and the relationship between event characteristics (duration, amplitude) and agreement levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database composition and event characteristics influence agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of the dataset (case mix) and the intrinsic characteristics of events/cases (e.g., seizure duration, signal power) strongly affect interrater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well-described, diverse databases and input from different expert types to improve generalizability; analyze and report how case features relate to agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured quality control for automated classification systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic classifiers should adhere to human decision rules, perform feature extraction and plausibility checks, include rule-based smoothing, and have a structured human expert quality-control step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare epoch-by-epoch agreement between system and human experts (report overall percent agreement and Cohen's kappa), and quantify variability introduced by human quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report benchmarking against human interrater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: When validating automated systems, present the automated-system vs human-expert agreement and compare it to interrater reliability between human experts to contextualize performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both system–expert kappa and human–human kappa; demonstrate whether system performance approaches or exceeds human agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate sample sizes and rater numbers; report statistical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability studies should include adequate numbers of participants, raters, and events; small sample sizes may yield nonsignificant changes despite qualitative improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report p-values for pre-post comparisons of kappa/ICC and acknowledge limitations due to sample size; consider multiple training sessions and larger samples for future studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize administration/instructions to improve reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and use standardized administration manuals or verbal instruction guides (example: standardized GDS-SF verbal manual) to increase interrater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the manual development process and empirically compare standardized vs non-standardized administration; report reliability improvements attributable to standardization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of reliability for clinical decision-making vs aggregate comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Some levels of interrater reliability (e.g., kappa ≈ 0.5) may be adequate for aggregate comparisons (comparing groups) but inadequate for reliable evaluations of single patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the intended use (aggregate benchmarking vs individual-level decisions) when judging acceptable reliability thresholds and adjust reviewer numbers accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider objectivity of source data when assessing reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability of abstractions (e.g., ICU admitting diagnoses, comorbidities) depends on the objectivity and clarity of source data in the medical record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which items had strong vs poor kappa and relate differences to data objectivity; use percent positive agreement for diagnostic abstractions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple raters and repeated scoring sessions to detect learning effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrater reliability may improve with repetition (a learned effect); studies should consider repeated scoring sessions to assess stability and training effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform multiple scoring sessions (e.g., one month later) and report changes in ICC/kappa; modify instructions/training if initial reliability is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report domain-specific considerations (age, context) affecting reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification reliability can vary by subgroup (example: professional interrater reliability improved for children older than 4 years) and by contextual knowledge required (e.g., pediatric fracture patterns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze reliability stratified by relevant subgroups (age, severity, disease type) and note when additional domain knowledge is necessary for accurate classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternative reliability metrics where appropriate (Kendall W, ICC for ranks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other statistics (Kendall's W for concordance, unweighted kappa, intraclass correlation for reliability of ordinal/continuous ratings) may be appropriate depending on scale type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the statistic that matches the measurement scale and report it with CI and p-values; explain choice (e.g., Kendall's W for multiple raters ranking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly define scoring/grading scales and thresholds for 'severe' or clinically meaningful categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Define cutoffs (e.g., mean motion score ≥ 4 = severe artifact) used for clinical or research categorization and report how consistently raters apply them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the scale description, examples for each level, and report percent agreement on clinically important thresholds (e.g., proportion where all readers assigned score ≥ 4).
